newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: WORLD BANK SEEKS FURTHER TIES.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BANK SEEKS FURTHER TIES.

text.p: Lithuania said on Monday that the World Bank was seeking further ties with the Baltic state as it attempts to complete its transition to a market economy.
The government made the comments after Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius met with Ruth Jacoby, the World Bank's managing director for the Nordic and Baltic region.
"During the discussion, further cooperation with the World Bank was discussed," the government said in a statement.
"The common opinion was reached that the World Bank can provide not only credits but it can serve as a data bank for the country," the statement added.
Lithuania has made clear its intention to wean itself from borrowing from international financial agencies such as the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
But it says it wants to continue cooperation in other spheres, such as information collection.
The country's past programmes with the World Bank have focused on the banking, energy and agricultural sectors, areas which observers say are in urgent need of reform.
